Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for taking this on. We're starting the last mile for our Azure offer and need a clear technical playbook that ties together runtime validation, provisioning for customer sandboxes, and the publisher account activation steps that gate co-sell eligibility. High-level asks: 

- A step-by-step runbook we can hand to our infra team for staging -> prod offer validation.
- Required service principal roles (least-privilege) that the Marketplace provisioning flow expects.
- Guidance on SKU mapping (metering-friendly SKUs) and any manifest fields that commonly cause rejections.
- Any blocking checks from the identity/tenant side (publisher tenant claims, SPN consent, publisher verification).

We have a staging subscription ready (sub-id: 3f7a-xxxx) and can create the SP if you confirm required perms. Also attaching our current SKU mapping CSV to show how we're structuring plans.

Attachments: nimbus-skus-mapping-v1.csv

Can we get a draft playbook and a 30-minute technical sync early next week? Prefer Tue/Wed morning PT.

Best,
Alyssa

NimbusAI

Subject: Re: Runtime validation & provisioning playbook for Azure offer (NimbusAI)

Hi Alyssa —

Appreciate the clear list. I've put together an initial draft playbook (attached) that focuses on the gated checks we've seen block offers: publisher identity, manifest SKU validation, service principal provisioning, and runtime smoke tests (cold-start / KV cache correctness / token throughput). Highlights in this draft:

- Preflight checklist (publisher tenant, SPN consent, required ARM role assignments).
- Staging provisioning steps (how to seed telemetry and create a sandbox customer instance via ARM template).
- Runtime validation tests (scripted curl/OpenTelemetry checks we recommend).
- Failure modes and quick remediation steps (expired certs, quota hits, manifest JSON errors).

Short answers to your specific Qs: 
1) Service principal roles: Contributor + User Access Administrator is overkill — we recommend a custom role with Microsoft.Resources/deployments/*, Microsoft.Web/sites/* if using App Services, and Microsoft.Insights/* for telemetry. If you're using VM/AKS, we'll list the exact actions in the playbook.
2) SKU mapping: your CSV looks fine; we'll map to meter-friendly SKUs (Per-User for seats or Per-Core for compute). I flagged a couple of plan names in the CSV that need consistent case and IDs to avoid manifest lint failures.
3) Publisher claims: you must complete tenant verification before identity-based entitlements (co-sell) will be allowed. We call this out in the preflight.

I've attached: redwood-azure-runtime-playbook-v0.9.pdf and service-principal-sample.json. Can we do Tue 15 Apr 2025 09:30 PT for a 30-min sync? I'll invite Karthik for the manifest/technical bits.

Attachments: redwood-azure-runtime-playbook-v0.9.pdf; service-principal-sample.json

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Runtime validation & provisioning playbook for Azure offer (NimbusAI)

Alyssa / team —

Quick technical notes ahead of tomorrow's sync: 

- Manifest gotchas: SKU id fields must be alphanumeric and match your ARM template parameter names. Avoid spaces and punctuation. Validate with the Marketplace linter (we include the CLI command in the playbook).
- Identity: For SPN we recommend using a client certificate credential (if your CI/CD supports it) rather than client secret to avoid secret rotation failures. The sample JSON I attached has the minimal actions we require for provisioning and telemetry patching.
- Runtime smoke tests: include a cold-start latency check, 99th percentile token latency goal (we recommend <250ms for runtime endpoints in Dedicated), and a KV cache consistency test. We'll provide a small harness script you can run in the staging sub to produce the pass/fail report.

I also added a short troubleshooting flow for manifest validation failures (common error messages and grep-able hints). See the playbook page 6.

On the call I'll demo the manifest linter and show the fail case for the SKU that contains a hyphen (that's the one that will likely be rejected).

—Karthik
Sr. Product Engineer, Marketplace Integrations
Redwood Inference

Alyssa —

Great — after the call we've updated the playbook to include the co-sell checklist and a lightweight acceptance checklist your team can sign off on. Quick answers: 

- Co-sell attributes: the manifest should expose plan-level entitlements and pricing metadata; include a marketplaceVisibility flag and a coSellEligible: true key in your internal mapping (this is used in the handoff to the field sellers — not strictly an ARM manifest property, but required by the publisher operations sheet).
- Entitlements: explicit entitlements are not mandatory in the manifest JSON itself, but your catalog metadata and the offer listing must reference the same plan IDs that you intend to route for co-sell. Consistency across manifest, ARM templates, and your offer UI is what gets flagged otherwise.

Next steps (action items):
- Marissa (me): I'll upload the updated playbook to your shared drive and send a DocuSign acceptance checklist for the provisioning run we performed in staging.
- Karthik: follow up with the manifest lint report and the sample SPN certificate guide.
- Alyssa: confirm whether you want us to run the runtime smoke harness (we can run it as a white-glove service for the first run).

DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/r/ABCD-1234 (acceptance checklist)

If you can sign before EOD Fri 18 Apr, we can schedule Redwood to run the harness on Mon 21 Apr and aim for offer submission the week after.

Thanks —
Marissa
